findings.title: Root login over SSH is disabled
findings.summary: root can log in with a password
findings.fix: Set 'PermitRootLogin no' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/50-hardening.conf, log in as a normal user with sudo, then run 'sshd -t && systemctl reload ssh'.

findings.title: Password authentication is disabled
findings.summary: passwords are accepted (brute-force target)
findings.fix: After confirming key-based login works, set 'PasswordAuthentication no' and reload ssh. Check files in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/ (cloud images often re-enable it there).

findings.title: Keyboard-interactive authentication is disabled
findings.summary: PAM keyboard-interactive login can accept passwords
findings.fix: Set 'KbdInteractiveAuthentication no' (ChallengeResponseAuthentication on older releases) unless you use it for two-factor login.

findings.title: Empty passwords are refused
findings.summary: accounts without a password can log in
findings.fix: Set 'PermitEmptyPasswords no' (the default) and give every account a password or lock it.

findings.title: No weak ciphers, MACs or key exchange algorithms
findings.summary: 5 weak algorithm(s) enabled
evidence: legacy but not broken: macs: hmac-sha1
findings.fix: Remove CBC/arcfour ciphers, MD5/SHA1-96 MACs and SHA1 key exchanges from Ciphers, MACs and KexAlgorithms, or delete those lines to use the OpenSSH defaults.

findings.title: MaxAuthTries is 4 or lower
findings.summary: MaxAuthTries is 6
findings.fix: Set 'MaxAuthTries 3' to slow down password guessing per connection.

findings.title: X11 forwarding is disabled
findings.summary: X11 forwarding is on
findings.fix: Set 'X11Forwarding no'; a web server has no use for it (Ubuntu's shipped sshd_config turns it on).

findings.title: LoginGraceTime is 60 seconds or less
findings.summary: LoginGraceTime is 120s
findings.fix: Set 'LoginGraceTime 30' so unauthenticated connections do not hold slots for two minutes.

findings.title: SSH logins are limited to named users or groups
findings.summary: no AllowUsers/AllowGroups: every account with a key or password can log in
findings.fix: Optionally add 'AllowGroups sshusers' (or AllowUsers) so new system accounts cannot log in by accident.

findings.title: A host firewall is active
findings.summary: no host firewall filters incoming traffic
findings.fix: sudo ufw allow OpenSSH && sudo ufw allow 'Nginx Full' && sudo ufw enable (allow your SSH port first).

findings.title: Incoming traffic is denied by default
findings.summary: no active firewall (see FW-001)
findings.fix: sudo ufw default deny incoming && sudo ufw default allow outgoing

findings.title: Listening network services (inventory)
findings.summary: 7 public and 2 local listening sockets
findings.fix: Stop services you do not need, or bind them to 127.0.0.1.

findings.title: Databases and internal services are not exposed
findings.summary: 2 internal service(s) reachable from the network
findings.fix: Bind the service to 127.0.0.1 (or a private interface) in its configuration and restart it; if it must listen publicly, allow only specific source addresses in the firewall.

findings.title: fail2ban protects SSH
findings.summary: fail2ban is not installed
findings.fix: sudo apt install fail2ban; Ubuntu enables the sshd jail by default. Check with 'sudo fail2ban-client status sshd'.

findings.title: Automatic security updates are enabled
findings.summary: unattended-upgrades is not installed
findings.fix: sudo apt install unattended-upgrades && sudo dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades (writes /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades with APT::Periodic::Unattended-Upgrade "1").

findings.title: No pending security updates
findings.summary: 2 security update(s) pending
findings.fix: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade (or wait for unattended-upgrades); then check reboot-required.

findings.title: No reboot is pending
findings.summary: a reboot is required to finish installing updates
findings.fix: Schedule a reboot (sudo reboot) so the updated kernel and libraries are used, or set Unattended-Upgrade::Automatic-Reboot "true" with a quiet Automatic-Reboot-Time.

findings.title: Package lists are recent
findings.summary: package lists are 40 days old; pending updates may be missed
findings.fix: sudo apt update; make sure APT::Periodic::Update-Package-Lists is "1" so this happens daily.

findings.title: The Ubuntu release is supported
findings.summary: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS is a supported LTS release
findings.fix: Upgrade to a supported LTS release (do-release-upgrade) or enable Ubuntu Pro for extended security maintenance.

findings.title: Network stack hardening (sysctl)
findings.summary: 5 of 16 network settings are not hardened
evidence: net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects = 1 (recommended 0: a server is not a router)
net.ipv4.conf.default.send_redirects = 1 (recommended 0: a server is not a router)
net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 0 (recommended 1: reverse path filtering against spoofing)
findings.fix:
Add to /etc/sysctl.d/60-hardening.conf:
  net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0
  net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects = 0
  net.ipv4.conf.default.send_redirects = 0
  net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 1
  net.ipv4.conf.all.log_martians = 1
then run: sudo sysctl --system

findings.title: Kernel and filesystem hardening (sysctl)
findings.summary: 1 of 9 kernel settings are not hardened
evidence: kernel.dmesg_restrict = 0 (recommended 1: only root reads the kernel log)
findings.fix:
Add to /etc/sysctl.d/60-hardening.conf:
  kernel.dmesg_restrict = 1
then run: sudo sysctl --system

findings.title: IP forwarding is off unless the host routes traffic
findings.summary: the host forwards packets but no container or VPN software was found
findings.fix: If this host does not run containers or a VPN, set net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0 in /etc/sysctl.d/60-hardening.conf; Docker, LXD and WireGuard need it on.

findings.title: No account has an empty password
findings.summary: 1 account(s) without a password
findings.fix: Lock the account (sudo passwd -l NAME) or set a password (sudo passwd NAME).

findings.title: Only root has UID 0
findings.summary: 1 other account(s) with UID 0
findings.fix: Give the extra account a normal UID (usermod -u) or delete it; use sudo for administrators.

findings.title: sudo asks for a password (no NOPASSWD rules)
findings.summary: 2 NOPASSWD rule(s) allowing every command
findings.fix: Remove NOPASSWD from the listed rules (cloud images add one for the default user in /etc/sudoers.d/90-cloud-init-users), or limit it to specific commands.

findings.title: No world-writable files in web roots
findings.summary: 2 world-writable path(s) in web roots
findings.fix: chmod o-w the listed paths (find WEBROOT -perm -0002 -exec chmod o-w {} +); give write access to the PHP-FPM user through group ownership of specific upload directories only.
findings.partial_reason: some directories could not be read

findings.title: setuid/setgid programs (review list)
findings.summary: 1 setuid/setgid program(s) writable by non-root users
evidence: setuid/setgid programs: 7, not on the Ubuntu default list: 2
known: mount, passwd, su, sudo, ssh-keysign
findings.fix: Investigate programs not installed by Ubuntu packages (dpkg -S PATH); remove the bit with chmod u-s,g-s if it is not needed. A setuid file writable by a non-root user is a root shell for that user.

findings.title: nginx hides its version (server_tokens off)
findings.summary: server_tokens is not set; nginx sends its version (default on)
findings.fix: Add 'server_tokens off;' to the http block of /etc/nginx/nginx.conf (Ubuntu ships it commented out), then 'sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx'.

findings.title: nginx allows only TLS 1.2 and 1.3
findings.summary: old protocols enabled: TLSv1, TLSv1.1
findings.fix: Set 'ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;' in the http block (Ubuntu 22.04's nginx.conf still lists TLSv1 and TLSv1.1) and in any server block that overrides it.

findings.title: PHP does not advertise itself (expose_php = Off)
findings.summary: X-Powered-By header sent by PHP 8.1 fpm
findings.fix: Set 'expose_php = Off' in /etc/php/VERSION/fpm/php.ini (or a conf.d override) and restart PHP-FPM.

findings.title: PHP does not display errors to visitors
findings.summary: errors are shown to visitors by PHP 8.1 fpm
findings.fix: Set 'display_errors = Off' and 'log_errors = On' in php.ini and in pool files (php_admin_flag[display_errors] = off), then restart PHP-FPM.

findings.title: MariaDB/MySQL is not listening on all interfaces
findings.summary: the database accepts connections from the network
findings.fix: Set 'bind-address = 127.0.0.1' in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf (or mysql.conf.d/mysqld.cnf) and restart; for remote access use an SSH tunnel or a private network with firewall rules.

findings.title: Redis is bound to localhost with protected mode on
findings.summary: Redis is reachable from the network: bound to a public address, protected-mode is off, reachable without a password
findings.fix: In /etc/redis/redis.conf set 'bind 127.0.0.1 -::1' and 'protected-mode yes', and require a password with requirepass or ACL users; then sudo systemctl restart redis-server.

findings.title: Swap is configured
findings.summary: no swap: memory spikes end in the out-of-memory killer
findings.fix: Create a swap file: sudo fallocate -l 2G /swapfile && sudo chmod 600 /swapfile && sudo mkswap /swapfile && sudo swapon /swapfile, and add it to /etc/fstab. Small VPS plans often have none, so the kernel kills MariaDB or PHP-FPM under memory pressure.

findings.title: Disks have free space
findings.summary: / 95% space used
findings.fix: Find large directories with 'sudo du -xh / --max-depth=2 | sort -h | tail'; clean old logs, backups, caches (apt clean, journalctl --vacuum-size=500M) or grow the disk.

findings.title: Filesystems have free inodes
findings.summary: / 85% inodes used
findings.fix: Find directories with many small files (sessions, cache, mail queue): 'sudo find / -xdev -type d -size +1M' and clean them up.

findings.title: The clock is synchronised (NTP)
findings.summary: time synchronisation is off
findings.fix: sudo timedatectl set-ntp true (systemd-timesyncd), or install chrony; TLS, logs and TOTP need a correct clock.

findings.title: The systemd journal has a size limit
findings.summary: the journal uses 3.5 GiB
evidence: SystemMaxUse not set (default: 10% of the filesystem, at most 4G)
findings.fix: Set 'SystemMaxUse=500M' in /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/size.conf, then sudo systemctl restart systemd-journald (or vacuum now: sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=500M).

findings.title: Root cron jobs do not run writable scripts
findings.summary: 2 root cron path(s) can be modified by other users
findings.fix: Make every script that root runs from cron owned by root and not writable by group or others (chown root:root FILE && chmod 755 FILE), including its directory. Run site tasks such as 'php artisan schedule:run' or wp-cron from the site user's crontab instead of root's.
